Gynecologic Oncology.question: 1) The most common gynecological malignancy in developed countries is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Endometrial carcinoma is the commonest gynecologic malignancy in developed countries.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 2) The most common gynecological malignancy in developing countries is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Cervical cancer remains the leading gynecologic malignancy in many developing countries, including Bangladesh.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 3) The most common histological type of cervical cancer is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for approximately 70–80% of cervical cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 4) Persistent infection with which HPV types is most strongly associated with cervical carcinoma?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: High-risk HPV types 16 and 18 are responsible for the majority of cervical cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 5) The transformation zone of the cervix is the site of origin for most:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Most cervical precancerous lesions and cancers arise from the transformation zone.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 6) The most common presenting symptom of cervical carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Postcoital bleeding is a classic early symptom of cervical cancer.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 7) The gold standard for confirming carcinoma of the cervix is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Histopathological examination of a biopsy establishes the diagnosis.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 8) The screening test most widely used for cervical cancer is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Cervical cytology is the standard screening method for cervical cancer.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 9) The Bethesda System is used for reporting:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: The Bethesda System standardizes reporting of cervical cytology.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 10) The investigation of choice for evaluating an abnormal Pap smear is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Colposcopy allows visualization and biopsy of abnormal cervical lesions.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 11) The most common route of spread of cervical carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Cervical cancer initially spreads by direct extension into surrounding pelvic tissues.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 12) The earliest lymph nodes involved in cervical carcinoma are:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Pelvic lymph nodes are the first regional nodes affected.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 13) The strongest risk factor for cervical carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Persistent infection with oncogenic HPV is the principal etiological factor.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 14) The most effective primary prevention of cervical cancer is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: HPV vaccination prevents infection with high-risk HPV types.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 15) The FIGO staging of cervical carcinoma is primarily based on:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: FIGO staging for cervical cancer is predominantly clinical, supplemented by appropriate investigations.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 16) A 35-year-old woman presents with postcoital bleeding. Speculum examination reveals a friable cervical growth that bleeds on touch. The next best step is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option1: Repeat Pap smear after six months
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Any suspicious cervical lesion requires histological confirmation.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 17) A woman has LSIL reported on cervical cytology. The next appropriate investigation is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Women with abnormal cervical cytology require colposcopic evaluation.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 18) A 45-year-old woman presents with foul-smelling blood-stained vaginal discharge and postcoital bleeding. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Blood-stained offensive discharge with contact bleeding is highly suggestive of cervical cancer.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 19) A woman with cervical cancer develops unilateral hydronephrosis. This finding corresponds to:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Hydronephrosis or a non-functioning kidney indicates Stage III disease.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 20) A woman with cervical carcinoma has tumor invasion into the bladder mucosa confirmed by cystoscopy. The disease is classified as:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Invasion of the bladder or rectal mucosa defines FIGO Stage IVA.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 21) A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with vaginal bleeding. TVS shows an endometrial thickness of 12 mm. The next most appropriate investigation is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Postmenopausal bleeding with thickened endometrium requires endometrial sampling.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 22) The most common histological type of endometrial carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma accounts for the majority of endometrial cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 23) The strongest risk factor for endometrial carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Prolonged estrogen stimulation without progesterone predisposes to endometrial carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 24) A 60-year-old obese diabetic woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Which diagnosis must be excluded first?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Obesity, diabetes, and postmenopausal bleeding strongly suggest possible endometrial carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 25) A woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding, obesity, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. Endometrial biopsy confirms endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The most important predisposing factor is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Type I endometrial carcinoma is estrogen-dependent and commonly associated with obesity and metabolic risk factors.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 26) The most common epithelial ovarian malignancy is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: High-grade serous carcinoma is the commonest epithelial ovarian malignancy.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 27) The most common route of spread of ovarian carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Ovarian cancer typically disseminates throughout the peritoneal cavity.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 28) The tumor marker most commonly associated with epithelial ovarian carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: CA-125 is useful for monitoring epithelial ovarian cancer, although it is not suitable as a screening test.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 29) The investigation of choice for the initial evaluation of a suspected ovarian mass is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: TVS is the first-line imaging modality for adnexal masses.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 30) The most common symptom of ovarian carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Ovarian cancer often presents late with abdominal distension, bloating, and increasing abdominal girth.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 31) A 58-year-old woman presents with progressive abdominal distension, early satiety, and weight loss. Ultrasound shows bilateral complex ovarian masses with ascites. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Bilateral complex adnexal masses with ascites in a postmenopausal woman strongly suggest ovarian carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 32) A woman with ovarian carcinoma develops a left supraclavicular lymph node enlargement. This represents:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Advanced ovarian carcinoma may spread via lymphatics to supraclavicular nodes.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 33) The definitive diagnosis of ovarian carcinoma is established by:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Histopathology after surgery provides the definitive diagnosis.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 34) The standard primary treatment for epithelial ovarian carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option2: Cytoreductive surgery followed by platinum-based chemotherapy
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Optimal debulking surgery followed by platinum-based chemotherapy is the standard treatment.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 35) The chemotherapy regimen most commonly used for epithelial ovarian carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Paclitaxel combined with carboplatin is the standard first-line regimen.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 36) A 24-year-old woman presents with an ovarian mass. Serum AFP is markedly elevated. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: AFP is the characteristic tumor marker of yolk sac tumors.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 37) A 19-year-old woman has an ovarian tumor associated with elevated LDH. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Dysgerminoma is commonly associated with elevated LDH.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 38) A 28-year-old woman has an ovarian tumor with markedly elevated β-hCG. Which tumor is most likely?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Ovarian choriocarcinoma secretes β-hCG.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 39) A woman presents with a solid ovarian tumor, ascites, and right-sided pleural effusion. Histology shows a benign fibroma. This syndrome is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Meigs syndrome consists of ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 40) A 52-year-old woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Ultrasound shows an ovarian mass, and endometrial biopsy reveals hyperplasia. Which ovarian tumor is most likely?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Granulosa cell tumors secrete estrogen, leading to endometrial hyperplasia and postmenopausal bleeding.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 41) The most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Dysgerminoma is the commonest malignant ovarian germ cell tumor.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 42) A 22-year-old woman presents with an ovarian mass and elevated LDH. Fertility preservation is desired. The most appropriate initial management is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Dysgerminoma is usually unilateral, allowing fertility-sparing surgery in appropriate patients.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 43) The tumor marker most useful for monitoring granulosa cell tumors is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Granulosa cell tumors characteristically secrete inhibin.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 44) A woman presents with vulval pruritus and a slowly enlarging vulval ulcer in her seventies. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Persistent vulval itching with an ulcerative lesion in elderly women suggests vulval carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 45) The most common histological type of vulval carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Approximately 90% of vulval cancers are squamous cell carcinomas.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 46) A woman with vulval carcinoma most commonly spreads initially to which lymph nodes?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: The superficial and deep inguinal nodes are the first draining lymph nodes.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 47) A 68-year-old woman has a persistent vulval ulcer that fails to heal after medical treatment. The next step is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Any persistent vulval lesion should be biopsied to exclude malignancy.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 48) The most common presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Postmenopausal bleeding is the classic presenting symptom.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 49) A 56-year-old obese diabetic woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy confirms carcinoma. The standard definitive treatment is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option2: Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and surgical staging
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Surgery is the primary treatment for most operable endometrial cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 50) A woman with epithelial ovarian carcinoma undergoes optimal cytoreductive surgery followed by chemotherapy. Which tumor marker is most useful for monitoring response and detecting recurrence?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Serial CA-125 measurements are widely used to monitor treatment response and recurrence in epithelial ovarian carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 51) The most common site of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) metastasis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: The lungs are the commonest site of hematogenous spread in GTN.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 52) The tumor marker used for diagnosis and follow-up of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Serial β-hCG measurements are essential for diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and detecting recurrence.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 53) The most common malignant gestational trophoblastic tumor is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Choriocarcinoma is the commonest malignant trophoblastic neoplasm.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 54) The hallmark histological feature of choriocarcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Choriocarcinoma consists of malignant trophoblast without chorionic villi.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 55) A woman develops persistent vaginal bleeding three months after evacuation of a complete mole. Serum β-hCG remains elevated. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Persistent elevation of β-hCG after molar evacuation strongly suggests GTN.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 56) The first-line treatment for low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Low-risk GTN is highly sensitive to single-agent methotrexate or actinomycin-D.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 57) The first-line treatment for high-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: High-risk GTN requires combination chemotherapy, commonly EMA-CO.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 58) A 26-year-old woman presents with persistent cough, hemoptysis, and markedly elevated β-hCG following a recent pregnancy. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Elevated β-hCG with pulmonary symptoms after pregnancy is highly suggestive of metastatic choriocarcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 59) The commonest malignant tumor of the fallopian tube is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Primary fallopian tube carcinoma is rare and is usually adenocarcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 60) A woman with ovarian carcinoma develops a hard umbilical nodule. This finding is known as:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: An umbilical metastatic nodule is called a Sister Mary Joseph nodule.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 61) A 48-year-old woman presents with postcoital bleeding. Examination reveals a friable cervical growth. Biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma confined to the cervix measuring 3 cm. The disease is classified as:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Disease confined to the cervix is Stage I.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 62) A woman with cervical carcinoma has extension into the upper two-thirds of the vagina without parametrial involvement. The FIGO stage is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Stage IIA involves the upper vagina without parametrial invasion.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 63) A woman with cervical cancer has obvious parametrial invasion but no extension to the pelvic wall. The FIGO stage is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Parametrial involvement without pelvic wall extension is Stage IIB.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 64) A patient with cervical carcinoma has tumor extension to the pelvic wall. The FIGO stage is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Extension to the pelvic wall is classified as Stage IIIB.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 65) A woman with persistent vulval pruritus undergoes biopsy, which shows vulval intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN). VIN is best described as:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: VIN is a precancerous lesion with the potential to progress to invasive carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 66) A 55-year-old woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy reveals atypical endometrial hyperplasia. The most important associated risk is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Atypical endometrial hyperplasia has a significant risk of malignant transformation.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 67) A 32-year-old woman is found to carry a pathogenic BRCA1 mutation. Which gynecological malignancy has the greatest increase in lifetime risk?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: BRCA1 mutations markedly increase the lifetime risk of epithelial ovarian carcinoma.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 68) A woman with hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome) is at increased risk of:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Lynch syndrome significantly increases the risk of endometrial and ovarian cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 69) A postmenopausal woman presents with abdominal distension and ascites. Ultrasound demonstrates bilateral complex adnexal masses, and CA-125 is markedly elevated. The most likely diagnosis is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Bilateral complex ovarian masses with ascites and elevated CA-125 strongly suggest advanced epithelial ovarian cancer.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 70) A 46-year-old woman with cervical cancer develops severe flank pain and hydronephrosis. The mechanism is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Cervical cancer may compress the ureters, causing hydronephrosis and impaired renal function.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 71) A woman with ovarian carcinoma has diffuse peritoneal deposits discovered during surgery. This pattern of spread occurs primarily through:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Ovarian cancer characteristically spreads by exfoliation of malignant cells throughout the peritoneal cavity.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 72) A 27-year-old woman has a unilateral ovarian mass with elevated AFP. Fertility preservation is desired. The preferred initial management is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option3: Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Fertility-sparing surgery is appropriate for many malignant germ cell tumors confined to one ovary.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 73) A 70-year-old woman presents with persistent unilateral vulval ulceration. The most appropriate next step is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Any persistent vulval lesion in an elderly woman requires biopsy to exclude malignancy.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 74) A woman with newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian carcinoma asks why screening is not routinely recommended in average-risk women. The best explanation is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option1: Available screening tests have not been shown to reduce mortality in average-risk women
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Routine screening with CA-125 and ultrasound has not demonstrated a mortality benefit in average-risk populations.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 75) A woman with Stage IB endometrioid endometrial carcinoma undergoes total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Histopathology confirms complete excision. Which factor is most important for determining the need for adjuvant therapy?
Gynecologic Oncology.option1: Final surgical stage and histopathological risk factors
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Decisions regarding adjuvant radiotherapy or chemotherapy depend on the final stage, grade, depth of myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion, and other pathological risk factors.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 76) The most common site of recurrence after treatment of epithelial ovarian carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Most recurrences occur within the peritoneal cavity due to transcoelomic spread.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 77) The most common malignant tumor of the vulva is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for about 90% of vulval malignancies.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 78) The most common presenting symptom of vulval carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Chronic itching with a vulval lesion is the commonest presentation.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 79) The definitive diagnosis of vulval carcinoma is made by:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Histopathological examination confirms the diagnosis.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 80) The most common histological type of vaginal carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Primary vaginal cancers are predominantly squamous cell carcinomas.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 81) A 47-year-old woman presents with intermenstrual bleeding. Speculum examination reveals an ulcerative cervical lesion. What is the next best step?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: A visible suspicious cervical lesion requires immediate biopsy regardless of cytology.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 82) A woman with Stage IA1 cervical carcinoma wishes to preserve fertility. The preferred treatment is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option4: Cervical conization (or simple trachelectomy in selected cases)
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Fertility-preserving treatment is appropriate for carefully selected microinvasive disease.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 83) A 34-year-old woman with Stage IB cervical carcinoma desires future fertility. Which treatment is appropriate in selected patients?
Gynecologic Oncology.option2: Radical trachelectomy with pelvic lymph node assessment
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Radical trachelectomy preserves fertility in selected early-stage cervical cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 84) The standard treatment for locally advanced cervical carcinoma (Stage IIB–IVA) is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy is the standard of care.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 85) A 61-year-old woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy confirms endometrioid adenocarcinoma. MRI shows disease confined to the uterus. The standard primary treatment is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Surgery is the primary treatment for most early-stage endometrial cancers.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 86) A woman presents with an adnexal mass. Ultrasound demonstrates a multiloculated solid-cystic lesion with papillary projections. Which feature is most suggestive of malignancy?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Solid areas and papillary projections are suspicious ultrasound features.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 87) A postmenopausal woman has a simple unilocular ovarian cyst measuring 3 cm with normal CA-125. The most appropriate management is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Small simple cysts with normal CA-125 can usually be monitored.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 88) A woman with epithelial ovarian carcinoma undergoes surgery. Which is the single most important prognostic factor?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Optimal cytoreduction significantly improves survival.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 89) A patient with epithelial ovarian carcinoma has omental metastasis. Which procedure is routinely performed during staging surgery?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Omentectomy is part of standard surgical staging and cytoreduction.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 90) A 16-year-old girl presents with a rapidly enlarging ovarian mass. Which ovarian malignancy is most likely in this age group?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Germ cell tumors predominate in children and young women.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 91) A woman with endometrial carcinoma asks why obesity increases her risk. The best explanation is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option1: Peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogen in adipose tissue
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Aromatization in adipose tissue causes prolonged unopposed estrogen exposure.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 92) A woman develops vaginal bleeding 18 months after menopause. Pregnancy test is negative. What is the diagnosis until proven otherwise?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Postmenopausal bleeding should always be considered malignant until excluded.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 93) A patient with cervical carcinoma develops severe pelvic pain and continuous urinary leakage. The most likely complication is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Advanced cervical cancer may erode into the bladder, producing a vesicovaginal fistula.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 94) A woman with advanced ovarian carcinoma is found to have pleural effusion containing malignant cells. This represents:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Malignant pleural effusion indicates distant metastasis (FIGO Stage IV).

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 95) A patient with cervical carcinoma develops para-aortic lymph node metastasis. The spread has occurred through:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Cervical cancer commonly spreads through pelvic and para-aortic lymphatics.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 96) A woman with ovarian carcinoma undergoes BRCA mutation testing. Identification of a BRCA mutation is important because it predicts benefit from:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: BRCA-mutated ovarian cancers are particularly responsive to PARP inhibitors.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 97) A patient with cervical carcinoma has extension into the lower one-third of the vagina without pelvic wall involvement. The FIGO stage is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Involvement of the lower third of the vagina defines Stage IIIA.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 98) A woman with epithelial ovarian carcinoma has markedly elevated CA-125 before treatment. Following surgery and chemotherapy, the CA-125 returns to normal. This most likely indicates:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Falling CA-125 levels correlate with favorable response, though recurrence still requires surveillance.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 99) A 63-year-old woman presents with persistent vulval itching and an ulcerative lesion. Biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. The primary route of lymphatic spread is to:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Vulval carcinoma first spreads to the superficial and deep inguinal-femoral nodes.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 100) A 58-year-old woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy shows atypical hyperplasia. She has completed childbearing. The most appropriate definitive management is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Hysterectomy is the definitive treatment for atypical endometrial hyperplasia in women who have completed childbearing.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 101) The tumor marker most useful for monitoring recurrence of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Serial β-hCG is the cornerstone of post-treatment surveillance.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 102) A patient with persistent postmenopausal bleeding has a benign endometrial biopsy but continues to bleed. The next appropriate step is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option3: Further endometrial evaluation (e.g., hysteroscopy with directed biopsy)
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Persistent bleeding warrants further assessment despite an initial benign biopsy.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 103) A woman with recurrent epithelial ovarian carcinoma develops bowel obstruction due to diffuse peritoneal disease. The mechanism is primarily:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Peritoneal dissemination commonly causes bowel involvement in advanced ovarian cancer.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 104) A 38-year-old woman with cervical carcinoma is HIV-positive. Compared with HIV-negative women, cervical cancer in HIV infection is generally:
Gynecologic Oncology.option4: More aggressive with higher persistence of HPV infection
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: HIV-associated immunosuppression increases persistent HPV infection and cervical neoplasia.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 105) The strongest prognostic factor in cervical carcinoma is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Survival is most strongly determined by the stage of disease at presentation.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 106) A woman with epithelial ovarian carcinoma has disease confined to one ovary with an intact capsule and no surface tumor. The FIGO stage is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Tumor limited to one ovary with an intact capsule and negative washings is Stage IA.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 107) A patient with Stage IA, grade 1 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma undergoes complete surgical staging. The most appropriate postoperative management is:
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Low-risk Stage IA disease usually requires no adjuvant treatment after complete surgery.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 108) A woman with cervical carcinoma presents with profuse vaginal bleeding causing hemodynamic instability. The immediate priority is:
Gynecologic Oncology.option4: Hemodynamic stabilization and control of hemorrhage
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Initial management follows emergency principles before definitive cancer treatment.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 109) A woman with ovarian carcinoma is found to have a BRCA1 mutation. Which additional malignancy is she at significantly increased risk for?
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: BRCA1 mutations markedly increase the lifetime risk of both breast and ovarian cancer.

Gynecologic Oncology.question: 110) A 55-year-old woman presents with postmenopausal bleeding. Examination, imaging, and biopsy confirm early-stage endometrial carcinoma confined to the uterus. What is the most appropriate definitive treatment?
Gynecologic Oncology.option3: Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and surgical staging
Gynecologic Oncology.exp: Surgery remains the standard definitive treatment for early-stage endometrial carcinoma.
